notes: The two 'the's of each 'the X of the house' phrase are placed by rule 29's arthrous-rectum counting: the present article takes the one standing before its own word and the construct takes the supplied one.

In 'the right side of the house', the head noun כֶּתֶף is a construct that can take no article, so the single written 'the' goes to the adjective's present article under rule 47's construct clause, not to the construct noun.
s023 קָדִים is the predicate of the כִּי clause and carries the construction-supplied copula 'was' (rule 20), with the supplied 'toward the' belonging to the adverbial noun (rule 33).
